rv.q: The energy and bravura of it all are frankly out of this world.
This eyeball-scorching, ear-blasting revival of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s train-racing musical-on-roller-skates is an audio-visual blitzkrieg, the like of which I’ve never seen before.
The most confounding question is how this bizarre juggernaut of a show pulls it off in spite of it all.
But my advice is to ignore the Ikea vibes, and let the songs transport you.
And it couldn’t be more ironic that in a show wholly about rivals fiercely racing to win, the missing elements are momentum and tension.
But “Starlight Express” is more theme park than theater.
It’s an awe-inspiring stadium gig-meets-theme park ride of a show – and it should be on track for a long, successful ride in its flash new home.
Hatley's design and the entire creative team have surpassed themselves.
It's full on, it's fun, and it's for kids.
A considerable amount more, as it transpires, starting with a coherent story and characters we can care about, no matter whether they are a “first-class observation car” (nope, me neither) or not.
If you're a musicals fan and consider yourself a kid at heart, you won't regret it.
...the production, inflatable costumes and all, is so busy ticking off pop culture references...

It’s a little like a truncated Eurovision song contest, you might hear the odd decent tune, but really, you’re only watching for the camp costumes and surreal staging, and it’s that which makes you want to choo-choo-choose this magical experience for your theatrical bucket list.
Big, bright and spectacular, this version of Starlight Express is sure to run and run.
A technically impressive feat, masking a somewhat flawed musical, but you are bound to leave with a smile on your face :)
The refashioned Starlight Express is a stunning visual spectacle and will be enjoyed as such.
What was to come was a high-octane, energetic wonder-fest.
